In this case, we use the double-angle formula for sine:

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta =2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,⇒\,\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2\theta =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .
$$

 

Letting $\theta =\frac{5x}{2},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡5x & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5x}{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5x}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /10}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5x}{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{5x}{2})\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /10}\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡5x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /10}\operatorname{sin}⁡5x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{[-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡5x]}_{0}^{\pi /10} \\  & =-\frac{1}{10}\operatorname{cos}⁡5x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /10} \\  & =-\frac{1}{10}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\cdot \frac{\pi }{10})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(5\cdot 0)] \\  & =-\frac{1}{10}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)] \\  & =-\frac{1}{10}\cdot [0-1] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
